Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important chase! The players are already in the middle. Aliya Riaz gets a promotion and will open alongside Muneeba Ali Siddiqi for Pakistan Women. Rosemary Mair to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the calculations have been made now. New Zealand Women just need a win to go through while Pakistan Women will have to chase down this total in 10.4 overs to make it to the semis. However, if they win after that point of time then India Women will qualify. All three teams are still in the race and this is a massive 20 overs or so coming up in this T20 World Cup. The Kiwis must have seen Pakistan Women giving no pace at all while the New Zealand Women batters used their feet a lot to counter that. It is going to be a battle and whoever can handle the pressure will come out on top. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Brooke Halliday is up for a chat. She says that it was hard work in the middle because the way Pakistan Women bowled. She says that a lot of slower bowlers were used by them and it was getting difficult for them to get going. Shares that they dropped a few catches at this venue so not a good ground in terms of catching but hopes that they can defend the target.

Pakistan Women, on the other hand, will be pleased with how they pulled things back after the Powerplay. However, things could have been a lot better if they didn't drop those 7-8 chances. Their bowlers were excellent creating opportunities and keeping the runs in check but they were not at all helped by the fielders. Nashra Sundhu was the pick of the bowlers with three wickets while Sadia Iqbal and Omaima Sohail chipped in with one each. Nida Dar got one on the last ball of the innings but should have had more as they dropped 3 easy catches on her bowling. Now it is up to their batters to step up in this big game.

The Kiwis got off to a steady start and even though the runs were not coming thick and fast, they didn't lose a wicket in the Powerplay for the third time in 4 games and scored 39 runs as well. However, once the fielding restrictions were lifted, they lost both the set openers and started to lose their way. The new batters found it really difficult to get going, and the runs dried up really fast. It was becoming more and more difficult to hit boundaries so the Kiwis made sure to run hard between the wickets and keep the scoreboard ticking. The partnership of 38 runs between Sophie Devine and Brooke Halliday has helped them post a fighting total here.

RUNS ON THE BOARD! This is exactly what New Zealand Women have at the halfway mark. Even though it may look like they are 10-15 runs short, the pressure will be on Pakistan Women as they not only have to win this but will have to chase this down really fast to give them a chance of qualifying for the semis.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! We can see the Pakistan Women's team in a huddle where a very emotional Fatima Sana Khan is giving a last-minute pep talk. Now, they spread out to take their respective field positions Suzie Bates and Georgia Plimmer are the two openers for New Zealand Women. It will be the skipper of Pakistan Women herself who has the new ball in hand and also has a great record against the Kiwis as well. Let's play...

We are almost ready but before this highly anticipated clash begins, players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be New Zealand's first followed by the national anthem of Pakistan Women.

PITCH REPORT - Lydia Greenway is pitchside. She says that it is very hot here in Dubai. Adds that there is a big gap between the square boundaries as one side is 53m and the other is 63m, and the straight hit is the biggest being 73m. Mentions that it is the same surface that was used in the game between New Zealand Women and India Women where the Kiwis posted a big total. She does not expect it to change much during the game. Carlos Brathwaite joins her and says that this outfield is more sand-based and diving and sliding properly will be key while fielding here.

Fatima Sana Khan, the captain of Pakistan Women shares that they need to play with NRR in mind. Mentions that they defeated New Zealand Women, last time they played them and are taking that confidence along. Ends by sharing that she comes in for Tuba Hassan as the solitary change.

Sophie Devine, the skipper of New Zealand Women says that they will bat first. Shares that they did a good job against India at this venue and hope to do well again. Adds that they need to play at their best against the strong Pakistan Women's side. Mentions that Fran Jonas comes in for Leigh Kasperek as their only change with Pakistan having more right-handers in their side. Ends by sharing that they are aware of what is at stake for them.

Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Muneeba Ali Siddiqi (WK), Sidra Amin, Sadaf Shamas, Nida Dar, Fatima Sana Khan (C) (In place of Tuba Hassan), Omaima Sohail, Aliya Riaz, Iram Javed, Nashra Sundhu, Sadia Iqbal, Syeda Aroob Shah.

New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Suzie Bates, Georgia Plimmer, Melie Kerr, Sophie Devine (C), Brooke Halliday, Maddy Green, Izzy Gaze (WK), Rosemary Mair, Lea Tahuhu, Eden Carson, Fran Jonas (In place of Leigh Kasperek).
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Sophie Devine. New Zealand Women have elected to BAT first.

Pakistan Women have struggled to find their rhythm in this tournament, winning just one match while losing the other two without much resistance. Their batting has been a major issue, with their key players yet to deliver. There’s no question about the talent in their lineup with Muneeba Ali, Nida Dar, and Aliya Riaz, but they’ve lacked the collective performance needed to shine. On the brighter side, their bowling attack has been impressive, with skipper Nida Dar leading the charge. Sadia Iqbal, Omaima Sohail, and Nida Sandhu have thrived in the spin-friendly conditions. This is essentially a knockout match for both sides, but Pakistan Women have a steeper challenge than the Kiwis. Who will secure the final spot from Group A alongside Australia in the semi-finals? Stay tuned, toss and team news coming up!

New Zealand Women kicked off their campaign with a commanding win over India, which is why their fate still rests in their own hands. Aside from the loss to Australia, their batting lineup has fired consistently, and with powerhouses like Devine and Bates in their ranks, they are a formidable side. The rise of young talent Plimmer has added depth to their lineup. Melie Kerr has been outstanding, especially with her all-round abilities, excelling with the ball, while Rosemary Mair has led the pace attack with great skill. The Kiwis look solid on paper and will be confident of sealing the deal in this crucial match.

Hello and a warm welcome, everyone! We’ve arrived at the penultimate game of the group stages, and it’s a massive one, not just because of the teams but because of the stakes involved. New Zealand Women are just one win away from securing their spot in the semi-finals, while Pakistan Women still have a slim chance of making it, but they’ll need to win by a huge margin. If Pakistan wins but falls short of the required margin, it will be India Women who will slip through to the semis. It’s a high-stakes encounter, and we can’t wait for the action to begin!
... MATCH DAY ...

The land of Emirates has treated cricketing fans worldwide with top drawer entertainment so far. Now as the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup, 2024 progresses ahead, Match 19 features another exciting and a crucial clash in Group A. Pakistan Women and New Zealand Women are all set to clash at the magnificent Dubai International Cricket Stadium. With teams down to their final games, the race for the top two spots in each group is heating up. New Zealand Women come into this match with momentum, having bounced back from a loss to Australia with a key win over Sri Lanka. They've notched two victories so far and boast a favorable net run rate, but currently find themselves in the third spot and need only a win to stay in contention of the top two in their group. Their batting success has largely hinged on the performances of Georgia Plimmer, Sophie Devine, and Melie Kerr, who have been the backbone of their innings. Melie Kerr in particular has stepped up as a sincere all-rounder as her contributions while bowling have proved to be pivotal for the team’s success. She stands join second in the leading wicket-taker’s charts and the team would expect its marquee player to keep up with these contributions. Young Rosemary Mair has impressed everyone with her bowling as well. Her 4-wicket haul against India paved their way to the win and the fact that she has been economical, makes her a an important bowler. Pakistan Women's campaign in this tournament has been plagued by underwhelming performances, with their sole victory coming against tournament debutants Scotland Women. Their path to qualification now seems as challenging as scaling a steep mountain. With only two points to their name, they find themselves in fourth place, facing potential elimination unless they can orchestrate a remarkable upset against the in-form White Ferns. Their record shows two losses while defending targets. However, the totals they set - 105 and 82 against India and Australia respectively - were far from competitive, offering little margin for their bowlers to work miracles. These statistics clearly indicate that Pakistan's batting has been their weakness, but since a long time now. Compounding their troubles is the absence of their full-time skipper, Fatima Sana Khan due to unavoidable circumstances at home. Her absence was a significant setback for the team, further depleting their reliable pace bowling options, especially considering Diana Baig's injury as well. But now, she is all set to return to the side for this do-or-die clash which will surely boost the side’s confidence. New Zealand Women will surely stride out as the favorites but their aim will be to defeat Pakistan Women by a huge margin to catapult their net run rate and zoom up to the top two. But, it will be this Pakistani side whose goal will be to bounce back strongly and salvage some pride. Although a lot of permutations and combinations will take place, irrespective, it is going to be an entertaining contest. Which side do you think will win this clash?
